title: The forward edge in the walking isomorphism is Kan anodyne
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and ordinary nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal J$ be the ordinary groupoid with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism for each ordered pair, and put $J=N(\mathcal J)$. Let $i:\Delta^1\hookrightarrow J$ be the nerve of the functor $[1]\to\mathcal J$ taking the vertices to $0,1$ and its unique nonidentity arrow to $0\to1$. Then $i$ is Kan anodyne: for every map $p:E\to B$ having the right lifting property against all horn inclusions $\Lambda_k^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$, $0\leq k\leq m$, every commutative square with $i$ on the left and $p$ on the right admits a diagonal filler. The assertion holds in each common input universe.

source.place: Subsection 3.1.2, Definition 3.1.2.1 and Remark 3.1.2.6 (horn-generated anodyneness and closure). The assertion about this particular edge is agent-formulated, not a quotation: its alternating-simplex horn filtration is recorded in report.md. Online source read 2026-10-17; WANTED archival copy. No Stacks tag states this walking-isomorphism result.

proof.text: Use the alternating-word filtration in [lem-coef-walking-isomorphism-alternating-horn-filtration]. Given a lifting square with the edge $i$ on the left and a map $p:E\to B$ having the right lifting property against every horn, lift first over the forward edge $J_1=i(\Delta^1)$. At each stage $n\geq2$, the new simplex is attached along $\Lambda^n_0\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, so the already constructed map on $J_{n-1}$ and the prescribed map to $B$ form a horn lifting square for $p$; choose its filler and glue it by the pushout property. The choices are compatible because each filler extends the preceding stage. Taking the degreewise union over $n$ gives a simplicial map $J\to E$ extending the original map on $\Delta^1$ and making the square commute. This is exactly the required diagonal filler.

source.place: Subsection 3.1.2, Definition 3.1.2.1 and Remark 3.1.2.6; horn-by-horn lifting along the explicit alternating filtration.

proof.text: The filtration node identifies $J$ with the ordinary nerve of the two-object groupoid and identifies $J_1$ with the nerve of the functor $[1]\to\mathcal J$ carrying its nonidentity arrow to $0\to1$, so the map used in Step 1 is the stated $i$. In each degree $J$ has finitely many simplices, and the filtration and compatible union are countable constructions in the common input universe. If $E$ is empty there is no map $\Delta^1\to E$ furnishing a lifting square; if $B$ is empty there is no map $J\to B$. Those cases are therefore vacuous. Step 1 constructs a diagonal for every square against every map $p$ satisfying the all-horn lifting hypothesis explicitly stated in the item. This is exactly its asserted Kan-anodyne lifting property.
